To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stimulation of single, identifiable brain cells of a marine mollusc elicits a variety of behavioral acts.
the nervous system of a simple marine invertebrate is composed of a few thousand neurons that can be mapped and that the behavior of the animal can be elicited by stimulation of single neurons.
the behavior of a complex animal is determined by the activity of a small number of large neurons and that the activity of each of these neurons is determined by the synaptic input it receives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how the nervous system of Tritonia is organized to generate behavior.
the mapping of the neural circuitry of Tritonia and the analysis of the behavioral acts elicited by stimulation of the mapped cells.
the mapping of the central nervous system and the correlation of the activity of individual nerve cells with the sensory and behavioral activities of the intact animal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nervous system of Tritonia is a highly organized and integrated system in which the individual components can be identified and studied in relation to the whole.
stimulation of the brain cells in Tritonia produces behavioral responses which are similar to those observed in the intact animal.
a single cell of the Tritonia central nervous system is capable of eliciting the entire behavioral repertoire of the animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain of this animal consists of a number of functionally independent systems.
a single cell can be identified in the intact Tritonia by its position in the brain, its morphology, its electrophysiological properties, and by its behavioral effects when stimulated.
the nervous system of this animal is not an amorphous mass of nerve cells and fibers, but is a discrete, highly organized, and identifiable network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a mystery.
the nervous system is not a mysterious black box, but rather a collection of individual cells that can be studied in isolation.
the brain of Tritonia gilgierti is not a black box.
